data.name: فتحة
data.note: A short a, written as a small stroke above the letter. The deck leaves most fathas out: a letter with no mark usually takes a, so حياة is still ḥayā.

data.name: كسرة
data.note: A short i, written as a small stroke below the letter.

data.name: ضمة
data.note: A short u, written as a small curl above the letter.

data.name: سكون
data.note: A small circle: this letter has no vowel after it. Spoken Palestinian drops many of the textbook’s short vowels, so a word can even start with two consonants: لْسان lsān (tongue) is lisān in the textbook, جْبين jbīn (forehead) is jabīn. Over و or ي the deck uses a sukun for the Palestinian ō and ē: موْت mōt (death), عيْلة ēla (family).

data.name: شدة
data.note: A small w-shape: say the letter twice, held longer. بنّ is bunn, coffee beans.

data.name: تنوين
data.note: A doubled fatha, usually on a final alif, adds -an. In speech it lives on in set words: شكراً šúkran (thank you), أبداً ábadan (never).
